dbms-ramakrishnan-3rd-edition/1nf.learnerSafeSummary: First normal form requires one value per cell, with no lists and no numbered repeating columns.
learnerSafeKeyPoints: A comma-separated list in a cell cannot be counted, filtered, or joined.
Numbered columns such as course_1 and course_2 hard-code an arbitrary limit.
Move repeating data into its own table with one row per value.
Each column should hold one kind of fact.

dbms-ramakrishnan-3rd-edition/2nf.learnerSafeSummary: Second normal form removes partial dependencies on part of a composite key.
learnerSafeKeyPoints: It only applies to tables whose primary key spans several columns.
A column depending on half the key gets stored repeatedly.
Move that column into a table keyed by what it truly depends on.
A join reproduces the original combined view on demand.

dbms-ramakrishnan-3rd-edition/3nf.learnerSafeSummary: Third normal form removes transitive dependencies, where one non-key column determines another.
learnerSafeKeyPoints: Storing a department name on every employee repeats it once per person.
It causes update, deletion, and insertion anomalies.
Move the dependent column into a table keyed by what determines it.
Most working schemas aim for third normal form.
